messages:
Maya: Quick heads-up — I put a first-pass PRD in the doc for the Observability Console work (dashboards, tracing UX, retention controls). Link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/PRD-OBS-1 :point_right:

Maya: Goal = give customers per-route/model dashboards, trace-level troubleshooting, and configurable retention with sane defaults. Launch = beta to 5 pilot customers, then GA after perf/scale sign-off.

Jonas: skimmed it — nice. Can we call out explicit acceptance criteria for query latency and dashboard load times?

Maya: yes — added an acceptance criteria section. TL;DR: dashboard initial render <= 800ms p50 on Dedicated, query tail p95 <= 2s for 30d retention dataset.

Alex: Backend note: 30d retention with full-span indexing will blow up disk IO for big customers. Need to define tiers and default sampling.

Priya: Customer asks we heard: (1) 90d retention for Enterprise, (2) stricter PII masking for logs, (3) audit logs exported to customer S3. We should map those to scoping/requirements.

Sam: UX questions — do we surface model-level traces by default or let customers enable? Prefer not to crowd the UI. Proposal: default = top-level request summary, with an opt-in toggle for full trace waterfall per model.

Jonas: agree with opt-in. For the rollout we can gate the heavy queries behind a feature flag + rate limit.

Maya: adding those. Also adding rollout plan: 1) internal dogfood + 2-3 paid alphas (opt-in), 2) enable GA for Dedicated customers with reserved capacity, 3) enable hosted tier with quotas and sampling.

Alex: acceptance criteria snippet I suggest adding to PRD:
```
- Metrics ingestion: no more than 10% increase in tail CPU on serving hosts for default config.
- Query SLA: p95 dashboard query <= 2s for <=30d retention on Dedicated.
- Data isolation: traces tagged with customer_id and never cross-tenant visible.
- Rollout safety: feature flag + canary for 10% of traffic for 48h with auto-fallback on error budget.
```

Maya: perfect. Needs an explicit migration plan for customers currently piping to internal dashboards. Also note the config UX: retention slider with presets (30d/90d/365d + custom).

Priya: add constraints for Enterprise: allow S3 export and KMS/HSM integration for retention export. Also include per-customer ingestion quotas and a billing knob.

Sam: I'll attach mock screenshots of the retention slider, sampling toggle, and trace waterfall flow by EOD.

Jonas: dev effort estimate — backend ~4w (indexing + retention + sampling), APIs ~1.5w, frontend ~2.5w, infra + rollout automation ~1.5w. Total ~9.5w of engineering. Need to buffer for perf tuning.

Maya: noted. Product-priority ask: which bits are MVP vs v1? Proposed MVP: dashboards (summary metrics + per-route), retention controls (30d default), trace search for last 7d, and export API. v1: 90d/365d tier, full trace waterfall, audit exports, KMS integration.

Alex: edge cases I want in PRD: (1) very high-cardinality models (per-model metrics explosion), (2) cross-tenant query attempts, (3) data backfill after retention changes, (4) partially failed export flows.

Maya: added those with acceptance criteria for each (e.g., backfill must be rate-limited and observable; failed export retries + DLQ).

observability-bot: [auto] Created issue OBS-1234: "Add retention presets + backend sampling" assigned to @Jonas.

Priya: for launch criteria we need: docs + runbook + support playbook + SLA language. Also eval plan with two synthetic workloads and one customer workload.

Maya: I'll draft the launch checklist: docs, runbook, beta cohort sign-off, perf benchmarks met, infra cost estimate, and legal review for retention/PII.

Jonas: can we include a lightweight query preview to show estimated cost per month for chosen retention/sampling? Helps customers pick configs.

Sam: UX: add tooltip with estimate and a link to "cost simulator" page. Keep it unobtrusive.

Maya: agree. Action items:
- Jonas: update PRD with infra configs + acceptance criteria (due in 48h).
- Sam: attach mocks (EOD).
- Priya: enumerate pilot customers and SLO requirements (48h).
- Alex: write perf test plan for canary (72h).
- Maya: finalize launch checklist and runbook (72h).

Jonas: noted. Also will add metrics for tracking post-launch (error budget burn, query latency, retention storage growth).

Maya: thanks all — quick sync tomorrow 9:30am, will post calendar invite. :calendar:

Alex: thumbs up.

Priya: :thumbsup:

Sam: :eyes:

Maya: Closing the loop here — ping me in thread for any blockers.
